name: Shiur of Forty Seah (Mikveh Minimum Measure)
notes: The requirement that a mikveh contain at least forty seahs of valid water; debates about what happens when a mikveh is found to be lacking

name: Drawn Water Invalidating a Mikveh (Mayim She'uvim)
notes: The rule that three logs of drawn water (mayim she'uvim) invalidate a mikveh; details of when and how this applies, including cases of doubt

name: Six Degrees/Categories of Mikveh Water
notes: The hierarchy of water sources for immersion: pools, cisterns, rain flows, springs, living waters, etc., each with different purifying capacities

name: Living Waters (Mayim Chayyim)
notes: Flowing spring water (mayim chayyim) required for purification of zavim, metzoraim, and preparation of mei chatat; distinguished from mikveh water

name: Hashakah (Connecting Two Mikvaot)
notes: The halakhic mechanism of connecting two bodies of water so that valid mikveh water renders drawn water valid; minimum hole size required (tube of a water-skin)

name: Color Change Invalidating a Mikveh
notes: Whether wine, olive sap, or dye that changes the color of mikveh water invalidates it; distinction between color change and actual mixing of liquids

name: Chatzitzah on Vessels (Interposition Blocking Immersion of Utensils)
notes: Materials (pitch, myrrh, clay, etc.) that block valid immersion of vessels; distinction based on whether the owner minds the substance being there

name: Chatzitzah on Persons (Interposition Blocking Immersion of People)
notes: Materials (threads, matted hair, pus, excrement, dough, clay) that block valid immersion of persons; rule that hidden or wrinkled parts do not require water penetration

name: Requirements for Valid Immersion of Vessels
notes: Specific requirements for vessels to be validly immersed: orientation in water, handles, knots, sealed containers, water entering inside; practical rules for tefillin, sandals, water-skins

name: The Sea as Equivalent to a Mikveh
notes: Dispute whether all seas are valid as a mikveh or only the Great Sea; whether flowing seawater is valid for zavim and metzoraim

name: Retroactive Unfitness of Mikveh (Lemafrea)
notes: When a mikveh is measured and found to lack forty seahs, all prior immersions are retroactively invalid; distinction between major and minor impurity

name: Snow, Hail, and Ice in a Mikveh
notes: Whether snow, hail, frozen dew, ice, salt, and thin mud can complete the forty-seah requirement of a mikveh; they supplement but do not invalidate

name: Other Liquids in a Mikveh (Juice, Wine, Brine)
notes: Status of grape juice, wine, brine, fish brine, and grape-skin wine that fell into a mikveh; whether they can supplement the forty seahs or invalidate

name: Spring Water (Ma'ayan) — Laws and Status
notes: Spring water purifies in any quantity when flowing; distinctions between a spring and a mikveh; what happens when a spring is channeled through vessels or troughs

name: Details of Seminal Emission Impurity (Keri)
notes: Details of what constitutes keri impurity: murky urine, white viscous fluid, heated flesh after a dream, drops from the member; timing of woman's discharge after intercourse

name: Purity Status of Mikvaot in the Land of Israel vs. Diaspora
hebrew: מקוואות ארץ ישראל לעומת חוץ לארץ
notes: Land of Israel declared clean; mikvaot of gentiles outside Israel valid for keri; within Israel, location relative to city entrance affects validity for different levels of impurity

name: Adjacent Mikvaot — Pooling Together (Hibur Mikvaot)
notes: Rules for when two adjacent mikvaot are considered joined (e.g., crack in wall, hole size); how water from one renders the other valid

name: Doubtful Immersion (Safek Tevilah)
notes: Status of person when there is doubt whether they immersed, or whether the mikveh had the required measure; distinction between doubt in public vs. private domain

name: Swallowed Objects and Immersion
notes: Status of a ring or other object swallowed by a person who then immerses or enters a tent of a corpse; whether the object is purified or remains impure after being vomited up

name: Effect of Immersion on Impurity Caused by Eating Unclean Foods
notes: Foods and liquids that cause bodily unfitness requiring immersion; the combining of all liquids for the quarter-log measure; whether immersion after eating unclean food removes the impurity of the food itself

name: Orientation of Vessels During Immersion
notes: A vessel immersed with its mouth downward is not validly immersed; vessels narrow at both ends or with inward-turned mouths require special handling

name: Bathhouse Pools and Mikveh Validity
notes: Rules regarding bath basins, their outlets, and the 'purifier' pipe in a bathhouse; when drawn water in the lower pipe invalidates the valid water above
